A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the surface chemistry of the porous carbon materials plays a key role in the catalytic performance, and the textural properties are also very important, especially in heterogeneous catalysis.
the use of carbon materials as catalysts or catalyst supports has increased in recent years due to their high stability and tunable properties.

we have developed methods for the functionalization of carbons with different chemical and textural features and have used these materials as supports for the preparation of catalytically active species.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the surface chemistry of the porous carbons can be tuned in a controlled way using a variety of chemical methods.
the surface chemistry and the textural properties of a porous carbon are interrelated and that the surface chemistry of a given carbon material can be tuned by modifying the textural properties.
the functionalization of the surface can be used as a powerful tool to tune both the surface chemistry and the textural properties.
